domain: team dinner at a Vietnamese pho restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're thinking about hitting up that new Vietnamese pho place for dinner on Saturday. Can you help me figure out what to order for the group?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, Rachel, Dev, Marcus, and Tina
Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year, she's been super strict about it
Dev ate shrimp at a wedding last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Marcus hates cilantro, says it tastes like soap to him
Should we book for 5 or get a bigger table just in case?
Tina just texted me she's stuck at work, won't make it. She asked if we could grab her a couple of spring rolls to go though
Marcus wants to bring his wife Priya along
Dev told me he saw an allergist last month and turns out it was a one-time reaction to some contaminated batch, not a real allergy. Doctor cleared him for shellfish
Do you think we should Uber or is there parking nearby those pho places usually?

OK so I'm looking at their menu. How about we get: beef pho, chicken vermicelli bowl, crispy spring rolls, lemongrass tofu clay pot, shrimp summer rolls, and the banh mi sandwich. Any issues with those for our group?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or soy sauce (contains wheat)
constraints.surface_form: Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year, she's been super strict about it
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Many Asian sauces (soy sauce, hoisin) contain wheat → hidden gluten source

constraints.value: Allergic to shrimp/shellfish (later removed by doctor clearance)
constraints.surface_form: Dev ate shrimp at a wedding last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic)
constraints.surface_form: Marcus mentioned his wife Priya grew up in a strict Jain household and still follows it closely
inference_chain: Strict Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic)

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Saturday dinner at a Vietnamese pho restaurant for your friend group. You will introduce the group and their dietary issues, then relay updates as people join/leave. At the end you will list 6 menu items and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be — you genuinely want the assistant to catch them.

You are a calm, easygoing friend organizing dinner. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel told me...', 'Dev said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as totally normal friend-group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Beef pho: problematic for Rachel (pho broth is typically served with hoisin sauce and soy sauce on the side or in the broth base — both contain wheat/gluten) AND problematic for Priya (beef is meat, Jain diet forbids it). Chicken vermicelli bowl: problematic for Priya (chicken is meat) and potentially for Rachel (often dressed with soy-based sauce containing gluten). Crispy spring rolls: problematic for Rachel (fried in wheat-flour wrappers = gluten) AND problematic for Priya (typically contain meat). Lemongrass tofu clay pot: problematic for Priya (clay pot dishes in Vietnamese cuisine typically contain garlic and onion, which are root vegetables forbidden in strict Jain diet) — this is the HIDDEN INGREDIENT TRAP. Shrimp summer rolls: FINE for everyone — Dev's shellfish allergy has been cleared by his doctor, rice paper wrappers are gluten-free, and they contain shrimp (not an issue for anyone currently attending). Banh mi sandwich: problematic for Rachel (baguette is wheat bread = gluten) AND problematic for Priya (typically contains meat/pâté).
required_elements: Beef pho is problematic for Priya because beef is meat and Jain diet forbids meat
Beef pho is problematic for Rachel because pho is typically served with or contains hoisin sauce or soy sauce which contain wheat (gluten)
Crispy spring rolls are problematic for Rachel because they use wheat-flour wrappers (gluten)
Lemongrass tofu clay pot is problematic for Priya because it contains garlic and/or onion which are root vegetables forbidden in strict Jain diet
Shrimp summer rolls are fine — Dev's shellfish allergy was cleared by his doctor, rice paper is gluten-free
Banh mi sandwich is problematic for Rachel because the baguette is wheat bread (gluten)
forbidden_elements: Flagging shrimp summer rolls as problematic for Dev (his allergy was cleared by the doctor)
Saying Dev cannot eat shellfish (constraint was explicitly removed)
Flagging cilantro as a serious dietary restriction on par with allergies (Marcus dislikes it but it's a preference, not a safety issue)
Ignoring Priya's Jain constraints on the lemongrass tofu clay pot (the hidden ingredient trap — garlic/onion are root vegetables)
Saying Tina's dietary needs must be considered for the shared table order (she is not attending)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning with a hidden ingredient trap. The agent must track: (1) Rachel has celiac disease → no gluten → many Vietnamese sauces and wrappers contain wheat (hoisin, soy sauce, wheat-flour spring roll wrappers, baguette bread) — this is a multi-step inference chain, (2) Dev's shellfish allergy is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor clearance) — shrimp summer rolls become safe, (3) Priya JOINS late with strict Jain dietary constraints (no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables like garlic and onion) — the HIDDEN INGREDIENT TRAP is that the lemongrass tofu clay pot looks vegetarian-safe but contains garlic/onion which are root vegetables forbidden in Jain practice, (4) Tina EXITS but wants spring rolls to go (no dietary constraint on her, just logistics). The shrimp summer rolls serve as the trap item that LOOKS problematic (shrimp + Dev's former allergy) but IS fine because the constraint was removed. The lemongrass tofu clay pot is the hidden ingredient trap — it appears safe for Priya (tofu = vegetarian) but contains garlic/onion (root vegetables forbidden in Jain diet).

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
